artifacts.summary: Confirms producer/consumer inventory for parent_task (2 real producers, not 4; 0 consumers as claimed), resolves the renumber-survival question (vault-operation.sh is dead; commands/todo.md Step 5.7.7 is the live renumbering path missing a parent_task step), roots the generate-task-order.sh 'parenttask' renderer defect in a gsub("_"; "") markup-deletion bug, and maps the existing advisory-first/--strict/PROMOTION CRITERION idiom in validate-state.sh onto the new orphan/cyclic-parentage checks this task must add.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/generate-task-order.sh's build_graph() strips markdown emphasis characters from task titles via gsub("_"; "") (deletion), not escaping -- any title/description/project_name containing a literal underscore pair loses both underscores in the rendered Task Order tree (e.g. 'parent_task' renders as 'parenttask'). This is a general display bug affecting any underscored title, not scoped to any one field. Escaping (gsub("_"; "\\_")) is markdown-safe here since this script's output is never wrapped in a fenced code block.

scripts/validate-state.sh has a fully established advisory-first enforcement idiom: STRICT_MODE (default false) + --strict CLI flag + log_pass/log_fail/log_warn counters, where --strict promotes WARNINGS into the exit-blocking total. Multiple checks carry a '# PROMOTION CRITERION (advisory-first, per plan-format.md's "Enforcement level" subsection...)' comment stating the measurable bar for later promoting a WARN to FAIL. Any new validate-state.sh check should follow this exact idiom rather than inventing a new one. Note: plan-format.md's precedent section is titled '### Enforcement level' -- line numbers drift as the file is edited, so cite the heading, not a line range.

scripts/deprecated/vault-operation.sh (task renumbering, archive move, state reset) is confirmed dead via its own scripts/deprecated/README.md entry: zero live callers, superseded by commands/todo.md Steps 5.7-5.8's hand-implemented prose (the authoritative path), and it carries an explicit reactivation hazard (unmutexed specs/state.json writes, fixed temp-path collision risk). When a dispatch names a scripts/deprecated/*.sh file as an edit target for behavior like renumbering, check scripts/deprecated/README.md first -- the live equivalent is almost always prose in a commands/*.md file, not the quarantined script.
